response.calorie_rationale: TDEE is about 1900 kcal and the provided target of 1650 kcal creates a modest deficit for weight loss while staying realistic for low activity and limited sleep. Higher protein intake is supported by the evidence for preserving lean mass during calorie restriction; 120 g/day is roughly 1.5 g/kg at 78 kg and fits the 1.2–1.6 g/kg range. The serving rows at 1600–1800 kcal also support a moderate pattern with 2.5–3.5 protein servings, 2.5–3 vegetables, 1.5 fruit, 2–4 whole grains, 3–4 dairy, and 3.5–4 fats.
response.meal_pattern: 3 meals + 1 protein-forward snack; aim for protein at each meal, vegetables at lunch and dinner, fruit once or twice daily, and whole grains in measured portions. Keep most carbs high-fiber and minimally processed; use dairy and healthy fats to improve satiety.
foods_to_prioritize: lean proteins (eggs, chicken, fish, Greek yogurt, tofu, soy foods, legumes)
vegetables, especially non-starchy and leafy types
whole grains like oats, brown rice, quinoa, whole-wheat bread
unsweetened dairy or full-fat dairy with no added sugars
healthy fats from olive oil, avocado, nuts, seeds
foods_to_avoid: refined grains like white bread, crackers, and packaged breakfast items
response.sleep_note: Sleep averages 6.1 hours, so keep caffeine earlier in the day, avoid very heavy late meals, and favor consistent meal timing to support energy and appetite control.
response.summary: This plan targets a modest calorie deficit for steady weight loss. Protein is the main priority to support fullness and lean mass, with high-fiber plants and whole grains for appetite and gut health. Keep meals simple and consistent, and avoid relying on refined carbs or sugary drinks. Improving sleep may also help energy and hunger control.
